meta.consequence: An exhibition that lands in the game log as a real result corrupts both teams' won-lost records, and everything built on them: RPI, the opponent adjustment, the resume view and the field projector.

meta.how_to_detect_later: A record that does not move. The feed carries each team's record on its NEXT match, so a team that played but whose record is unchanged played an exhibition. That is a real after-the-fact check and it is how this file should be audited, not extended by guesswork.
meta.note_on_use: Excluded from records and ratings, NOT hidden. Cody's point is that a match against good opposition still tells you something about a team even when it does not count.
sources: Cody, 2026-08-27: these are exhibitions and do not count toward W/L
meta.why: The feed does not mark exhibitions. Checked game 6640217 directly: no type, gameType or exhibition field exists, division reads 1, and both teams show record (0-0) -- it is indistinguishable from a counting match. So these are recorded by hand, with a source, rather than inferred from anything.
meta.why_it_cannot_count: ⚠ THE FORMAT IS THE PROOF, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN ANY ARTICLE. NCAA playing rules put a set at 25 points. A set played to 21 is therefore not an NCAA match, whatever anyone writes about it -- and no source I could find states the exhibition status outright, so this is the evidence that actually settles it.
meta.why_the_stats_are_poison: ⚠ AND EXCLUSION IS NOT OPTIONAL, IT IS ARITHMETIC. Every rate this hub computes is PER SET: points per set, kills per set, swings per set, the opponent adjustment, the rally model. A 21-point set offers roughly 16% fewer points than a 25-point one, so folding these in would quietly deflate the per-set numbers of four of the best teams in the country and nothing on screen would look wrong.
